title: Removable Discontinuity: A Hole in the Graph
caption_md: This plot shows $f(x) = \frac{x^2 - 4}{x - 2}$, which simplifies to $x + 2$ everywhere except at $x = 2$, where the function is undefined. The open circle marks the **removable discontinuity** (hole) at $(2, 4)$. Notice the two-sided limit $\lim_{x \to 2} f(x) = 4$ exists, but $f(2)$ is not defined — this is what makes the discontinuity removable rather than a jump or infinite discontinuity. Compare: a **jump** discontinuity would show two different finite values from the left and right, while an **infinite** discontinuity would show the curve blowing up toward $\pm\infty$ (a vertical asymptote).
